What is ClickUp Brain?

AI layer across the ClickUp work management platform - it answers questions about tasks, docs and people, generates status updates and standups automatically, and runs autonomous agents that act on tasks based on triggers.

Best for

Turning live project data into status updates and automated task actions.

Main features

  • Ask AI across tasks, docs, chat and connected apps
  • AI StandUp and automatic progress rollups
  • AI-generated subtasks and task descriptions
  • AI Notetaker for meetings
  • Autopilot Agents triggered by task events
  • Brain MAX desktop app with voice input and multi-model access (GPT, Claude, Gemini)
  • AI writing in Docs
  • AI fields in tables.

Practical use cases

  • Generating a weekly status report from live task data without chasing anyone
  • auto-creating subtasks from a project brief
  • answering 'what is blocking release 2.4' from task history
  • transcribing and assigning actions from a meeting.

Who is it for?

  • Project managers, agencies, operations teams and mid-size companies using ClickUp as their work platform.

Pricing, free access & limits

Per-seat add-on on top of a ClickUp plan; also bundled in some tiers

Plans described in the source

ClickUp Free Forever $0 (no Brain). Unlimited around $7/user/mo annually ($10 monthly). Business around $12/user/mo annually ($19 monthly). Enterprise custom. ClickUp Brain is sold as an add-on at roughly $5-9/user/mo on top of any paid plan; ClickUp has periodically bundled Brain into higher tiers or run unlimited-AI promotions. Brain MAX is priced separately at a higher rate. Verify - ClickUp changes AI packaging frequently.

Free plan

ClickUp itself has a genuinely generous free tier, but Brain is not included in it.

Free trial

Yes - free trials of Business and Brain are offered; ClickUp runs frequent promotional AI trials.

Usage limits to consider

Brain requires a paid ClickUp plan - it is not available on Free Forever. AI usage has historically been subject to per-seat monthly limits on some packagings and unlimited on others.

Strengths & tradeoffs

These points summarize the supplied research, rather than hands-on test results.

Strengths noted in the source

  • Grounded in live project data, so status rollups reflect reality rather than what someone remembered to write
  • AI StandUp genuinely eliminates a recurring meeting for some teams
  • Brain MAX giving multi-model access plus workspace context is an unusual combination
  • ClickUp's base platform is feature-rich and cheap.

Limitations to consider

  • ClickUp's overall product is notoriously heavy and slow, and Brain inherits that
  • AI packaging has changed repeatedly making cost planning hard
  • answer quality depends on task hygiene, which is poor in most real workspaces
  • the sheer surface area of features makes adoption difficult
  • performance issues on large workspaces are a persistent complaint.

Platforms, languages & integrations

Platforms

  • Web, Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, Android, Chrome extension, Brain MAX desktop app

Languages

  • Interface in 10+ languages; AI output multilingual

API access

Yes - ClickUp API v2/v3 with webhooks

Integrations and exports

  • Slack, Google Drive, GitHub, GitLab, Figma, Zoom, Microsoft Teams, Outlook, Salesforce, HubSpot, Zapier, Make, 1,000+ via integrations

Evaluation notes

Brain's output quality is a direct function of whether your team actually keeps tasks updated - it cannot summarise data that was never entered. Pilot on one well-disciplined team before a company rollout.
